name: Hotel Madame Reve
positioning: Independent hotel in the 1888 Louvre Post Office building in Paris's 1st arrondissement, with a planted rooftop and rooms looking over the city's rooftops and monuments
best_for: Travelers who want a central Paris base near the Louvre and Palais Royal
Guests who want a room with a terrace or balcony and city views
Travelers drawn to a hotel in a historic post office building

facts.text: The hotel is set in the building of the Louvre Post Office.
The building dates back to 1888 and was the city's first 24-hour post office.
The hotel is in Paris's 1st arrondissement, a stone's throw from the Louvre and the Palais Royal.
The Bourse de Commerce and the Samaritaine are also a stone's throw from the hotel.
Rooms are dressed in walnut woodwork, warm velvet and bespoke zelliges, in a setting inspired by Art Nouveau.
Most rooms and suites have terraces or balconies with views of Parisian rooftops and monuments.
Garden View rooms and suites have an outdoor space overlooking the hotel's suspended garden.
The 150-square-metre wellness area has two treatment cabins, a sauna with views over Paris and a fitness room.
La Plume is a rooftop restaurant with a tree-lined terrace and views of Saint-Eustache church and the Eiffel Tower.
Solar panels produce part of the hotel's hot water.
The hotel was founded by French entrepreneur Laurent Taieb.
There are no steps, and all rooms, restaurants and lounges are reachable by elevator.

highlights.text: The ROOF rooftop covers 1,000 square metres, set among cherry trees and lush greenery.
The rooftop is reserved for hotel guests during the day and opens to all in the evening for cocktails.
The 130-square-metre Penthouse is designed like a Parisian apartment suspended above the city.
Rooms and suites offer panoramic views over Paris, including the Eiffel Tower and Montmartre.
Some 800 pieces of mail art hang throughout the hotel.

considerations.text: In the evening the rooftop is open to the public, not only to hotel guests.
The wellness area is 150 square metres, with two treatment cabins.
WhataHotel notes a busy central Paris location with urban noise.
